title: Should We Move Closer to the Stream?

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A couple disagree about moving their hut closer to the stream: keep talking, or try a compromise.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) have been talking for weeks about moving their hut closer to the stream. (subject) wants to: fresh water, cool shade, the sound of running water at night. (friend) doesn't: the stream floods sometimes, and (friend.he/she) likes their sea view. Tonight they're talking about it again.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: They talk until late. Neither changes the other's mind. Finally (subject) says, "Can we just not decide? For now?" (friend) nods, relieved. They don't move. They don't stop talking about it either, now and then. It's one of those things couples carry around for years. It doesn't seem to do them any harm.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: "What if we keep the hut," says (friend), "and build a little shelter by the stream, for hot afternoons?" (subject) thinks about it. It's not what (subject.he/she) wanted. It's not what (friend) wanted either. They build it. It turns out to be (friend)'s favorite place on the island, which (friend.he/she) is a bit embarrassed about.
